What do you think?

So the issue of selecting the right people is a little bit challenging, but I think can be done. You just need a lot of people, you need to have a large group of people who are willing to participate, and then you can select people for particular tasks that they're good at. I think one harmful thing is just selecting the wrong person just because they're interested, right? So yeah, it depends on what specific tasks that they're doing.

I think generally I'm good at selecting people, right? Look at my friends. But is there anything better than what we're thinking about doing for yourself than this?

I still think that we're undervaluing the labor theory of robotics. But other than that, I think it's good. I think that basically what you're doing is you've articulated what Gramsci articulated, that memetics is the most influential component in the system, and you don't need to actually control the means of production or the means of compute in order to control the system. You can just influence memetics, and I think that's correct. So I think Gramscian Marxist analysis applied to AI makes a lot of sense. I just think that any Marxist theory without a theory of labor, which would be robotics in this sense, just doesn't really make... It's just like, who's going to make the shit? And who's going to control who makes the shit? That's a very, very important part. And so I think that grand level theories are good, but below that, you need to have practical theories about how stuff gets made. Who owns the robots? Who owns the intelligence? I think this is something that is underexplored, but it's a subcategory.
